summary: A 153-line inactive geometric input reconstructs the negative-bundle logarithmic weight of Kusakabe and Matsumura arXiv:2610.12175v1. It proves a psh exhaustion, a Kähler form dominated by the logarithmic Levi form, absence of radial critical points, the exact zero-section multiplier ideal and sharp jet-vanishing threshold, and a complete Kähler metric on the punctured total space. The compact-base case separates strict positivity off the zero section from the Stein property. Two complete final manual reads and 32 mathematical obligations pass. All420 book files, both catalogue files and both original manifests remain exact to658.

mathematical_obligations.check: The base may be noncompact, but must have the stated smooth nonnegative psh exhaustion and Kähler form.
The chosen Hermitian metric has a uniform Griffiths-negative bound with respect to the specified base form.
The curvature is unscaled; the book operator satisfies 2πddc=i∂∂bar, while the primary paper uses the unscaled operator.
A Chern-normal unitary holomorphic frame exists at any chosen base point by the existing internal lemma.
The first base derivatives and mixed base/fiber derivatives of the squared norm vanish in this frame.
The horizontal Hessian of U is minus the curvature paired with v, and its vertical block is the fiber metric.
The negative curvature bound makes U psh everywhere and strictly psh off the zero section.
The log U Hessian has horizontal lower bound ω and vertical Cauchy–Schwarz remainder.
The remainder is nonnegative and annihilates the radial vertical complex line.
Ω is positive on both base and fiber even on the zero section.
Ω is smooth and closed because the base form is Kähler.
log q=log U+U, so its unscaled Levi form dominates Ω off the zero section.
Exponentiation makes q strictly psh off the zero section.
The local norm equivalence gives log q=log|v|²+O(1) and an upper-limit value minus infinity on Z.
The internal analytic removable-singularity lemma proves the psh extension.
A Ψ sublevel lies over a compact base sublevel and in a compact metric disk bundle; it is closed.
The real radial field differentiates U to 2U and q to 2(1+U)q.
The nonzero radial derivative excludes critical points off Z.
The zero section has complex codimension equal to the bundle rank r.
The existing multiplier-ideal formula gives max(floor(m)-r+1,0), with the original e^-mφ convention.
A fiber term of degree a is integrable exactly when a+r>m; equality is logarithmic divergence.
The threshold m≥r+k-1 guarantees k-jet vanishing; below it a monomial of degree k-1 is integrable.
Smooth positive volume factors do not change this local threshold.
A smooth convex increasing extension of -log(-t) from t≤-1 exists.
The composed η(log q) has nonnegative Levi form off Z, so the proposed metric is smooth Kähler there.
The Ψ² barrier controls the gradient of Ψ uniformly and excludes finite-length escape at infinity.
The second derivative η″=1/t² controls the gradient of τ=log(-log q) where t=log q≤-1.
τ tends to infinity at Z, excluding the remaining finite-length escape; no completeness of Ω itself is claimed.
A direct sum of inverse positive line metrics has curvature exactly -ω times the identity.
On a connected compact positive-dimensional base, holomorphic functions are constant on the zero section, so the total space is not Stein.
The metric and exhaustions concern E and E minus Z; no improved convexity index of the projective completion U_E is asserted.
No Oka globalization, Nakano vanishing, Demailly weighted L² existence theorem or algebraic-reduction theorem is adopted by these elementary arguments.
